name: Sacred Mountain Sulaiman-Too
near: Osh: the mountain stands in the center of the city; the main entrance is on Gapar Aitiev St. at the intersection with Shota Rustaveli St. (eurasia.travel); the museum is at 71/2 Gapar Aitiev St. (2GIS).
elev: About 1,175 m — the highest peak, Rushaan-Too; the mountain rises about 200 m above the city and is about 1.5 km long (eurasia.travel; some sources give 1,172 m for the mountain as a whole).
short: Sulaiman-Too is a five-peaked sacred mountain in the center of Osh, Kyrgyzstan’s first UNESCO World Heritage site (2009): pilgrim paths, caves, petroglyphs, “Babur’s house” and a cave museum.
desc: The sacred mountain Sulaiman-Too has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2009. A rocky massif about 1.5 km long rises about 200 m above Osh and has five peaks: Takhti-Sulaiman (Buura-Too), Shor-Too, Kattama-Too, Rushaan-Too (the highest, ~1,175 m) and Eer-Too (eurasia.travel). On the mountain there are places of worship, caves, petroglyphs and polished rock “slides” used in healing and fertility rituals; on the main peak is the reconstructed “khujra” (house) of Babur, built in the late 15th century by the future founder of the Mughal Empire, destroyed in the 1950s and restored from photographs (eurasia.travel, travel-tramp). A cave museum was opened in the mountainside in 1978; the National Historical and Archaeological Museum Complex “Sulaiman-Too” (founded in 1949) holds about 33–35 thousand exhibits (24.kg, 2025). About 300,000 people visit the mountain a year; from October 2026 to the end of 2028 a reconstruction costing ~$12 million (the World Bank) is under way: the cave, ethnographic and archaeological museums, three entrance zones (Suu-Darbaza, Ot-Darbaza, Too-Darbaza), a visitor center, staircases and lighting will be renovated; there are no plans to close the site completely (Kaktus, 01.07.2026).
guide: Climb from the east side — up the steps straight to “Babur’s house” on the summit: the climb takes 15–25 minutes, and from the top all of Osh lies in the palm of your hand. Notice the stones polished to a shine: these are the “slides” down which women asking for children and pilgrims who believe in healing have slid for centuries. Descend by the gentle road to the west, to the cave museum — the exhibition is built right into a natural cave — and to the large mosque at the foot. It is best to come at dawn or sunset: it is cooler and the light over the city is beautiful. Since autumn 2026 a reconstruction has been under way — some areas may be temporarily fenced off.
see: The five peaks and the pilgrim paths; “Babur’s house” (khujra) on the Takhti-Sulaiman peak; the ritual “slides” and caves; petroglyphs; the mausoleum of Asaf ibn Burkhiya at the southeast entrance (vitalik.kz); the cave museum and the historical and archaeological museum complex; viewing platforms with a panorama of Osh; the large mosque at the western foot; a medieval bathhouse (24.kg).
skip: You dislike stairs in the heat — in summer at midday the climb is hard (travel-tramp). You are looking for wild nature — this is an urban shrine with paved paths. You come in 2026–2028 for the museums — some exhibitions may be closed for reconstruction.
diff: Easy: paved paths, steps and handrails; to the upper platform ~15–25 min (TripAdvisor; vitalik.kz). In places the stones are polished and slippery, and some steps are damaged (TripAdvisor).
when: Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–October): blossoms and a comfortable temperature (vitalik.kz — March). In summer at midday it is hot on the open slopes (travel-tramp). Accessible year-round.
hours: Museum: 09:00–17:30 per 2GIS (2026); other sources say 09:00–18:00, Tuesday–Sunday, Monday closed (kupi.com, year not given); the museum is sometimes closed after lunch (TripAdvisor reviews). The mountain: daytime visits; since 2024 night entry has been restricted (TripAdvisor review, 04.2024). From 10.2026 — a phased reconstruction with temporary closure of individual zones (Kaktus, 2026).
daytime: Sunrise or sunset — coolness and the best views of the city (TripAdvisor); the museum — before lunch, while it is surely open.
how: The mountain is in the center of Osh: on foot from the center/Jayma bazaar; by taxi (Yandex Go, inDrive) to the entrance on Gapar Aitiev St. at the intersection with Shota Rustaveli St. For cars — paid parking; the barrier is opened for tour buses/taxis for an extra fee (eurasia.travel). There are no entrances on the north side (vitalik.kz).
needcar: No: on the mountain — on foot only; you can walk to the entrance from the center or get there by taxi/city transport.
self: Yes: the route is well equipped, with map boards at the entrances (vitalik.kz). A guide is needed only for a detailed story about the shrines and petroglyphs.
roadtype: City streets to the entrance; on the mountain — paved paths and steps with handrails; the western slope — a gentle road (travel-tramp, TripAdvisor).
traveltime: From the center of Osh — 5–15 minutes by taxi or 15–30 minutes on foot (editorial). The climb to the summit — 15–25 minutes; a full visit with the museum — 2–3 hours (editorial, per reviews).
stay: Hotels and guesthouses of Osh within walking distance (the city center). Specific hotels have not been checked within this card — look on Booking/2GIS.
net: Osh’s city 4G coverage by all operators (Beeline, O!, MegaCom) — no specific complaints about a lack of signal on the mountain were found (editorial; specific coverage maps were not checked).
entry: A ticket to the complex grounds — 70 som (Kaktus, 01.07.2026). The museum — a separate fee: 150 som for foreigners (travel-tramp, year not given); kupi.com says “about 30 som” (probably an outdated price for citizens). Old reviews (2018) — 20 som for the mountain. The current 2026 museum tariffs are not confirmed.
transfer: Not required for a visit on foot; taxis in Osh — at Yandex Go/inDrive rates (prices not checked). Parking is paid, the amount was not found.
bring: Comfortable non-slip shoes (the stones are polished); water and a hat in summer; modest clothing — this is a sacred place (shoulders and knees covered; editorial); cash som for tickets.
warn: An active shrine: respect those praying, and do not photograph people during rituals without permission. Stories about healing belong to belief; medical effectiveness is not confirmed. Slippery polished stones and damaged steps — be careful with children (TripAdvisor). From October 2026 to the end of 2028 — reconstruction: temporary restrictions in individual areas are possible (Kaktus, 2026). Night entry is restricted (2024).
food: Osh plov and southern samsa — in the teahouses of central Osh and by the Jayma bazaar (editorial; specific establishments not checked).
reviews: Google Maps: 4.6/5, 335 ratings (the mountain, 03.10.2026). 2GIS (the “Sulaiman-Too” museum): 4.9/5, 739 ratings, 127 reviews (07.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Mountain Sulaiman-Too”: 4.2/5, 192 reviews, No. 1 of 23 in Osh. Pros: an easy climb, a panorama of the city, history, the museum. Cons: slippery stones, damaged steps, the museum closed after lunch, restricted night entry.
p.sum: The mountain is in the center of Osh: get there by Yandex Go to “Gapar Aitiev 67” (the Aitiev–Rustaveli intersection) or walk from the Jayma bazaar. The best route is to climb from the western (gentle, by the mosque) entrance and descend the steep eastern staircase to the museum; ~1.5 h for everything. A ticket for the mountain is 70 som, the cave museum and the state museum another 70 som each. From October 2026 to the end of 2028 a reconstruction is under way — some areas are fenced off, the mountain is not closed.

p.season: May–August: open 08:00–22:00, hot in the daytime — go at 09:00 or after 16:00. April, September, October: 09:00–19:00, the best weather. November–March: 09:00–18:00. From 10.2026 to the end of 2028 — a phased reconstruction of the entrances (Suu-Darbaza, Ot-Darbaza, Too-Darbaza), the museums and the staircases.

p.permits: Not needed. A ticket for the mountain is 70 som (Kaktus 07.2026; asocialnomad 09.2026); the cave museum 70 som, the state museum 70 som (separate tariffs may apply to foreigners — earlier 150 som). It is forbidden to bring plastic bottles, bags and disposable tableware. Modest clothing at the holy places.
p.access: With children — yes. For older people — the western gentle climb; the eastern staircase is steep. Stroller — difficult, steps; golf carts are promised after the reconstruction. Dogs — not advisable (a shrine).
